title: Write Jira comments with AI: post a clear test update
h1: put a clear test update on a jira issue
description: Turn test notes into a Jira comment with an AI bot. Review formatting, check who can see it and approve the comment before it reaches the issue.
answer: **give the next person enough detail to repeat your test.** a bot turns your notes into a jira comment with steps, links and a clear result. it finds the issue from the project and problem you name. posting counts as a send and asks first by default. read the wording and audience before you approve.

review.by: lead agent, after two independent reviewer passes, against Metal docs and the composio catalog

og_line: test evidence where the team can read it.
what:
**put the evidence beside the issue.** the bot finds the work through jira search, then prepares a comment. it supports lists, bold text and mentions. clickable links need words attached, not bare web addresses.

you can limit a comment to a project role or group. check the actual names first. group restrictions need an administrator to enable them. if the audience can't be confirmed, stop.
uses: **show how checkout failed.** include the steps and observed result.
**leave a release check people can follow.** use links with descriptive words.
**keep an investigation within its audience.** confirm the existing project role first.
**answer with evidence.** separate expected behaviour from what you actually saw.

routine.message: every thursday at 4, find issues in the payments project that moved to done this week and have no comment from the last seven days. for each one, write a short comment asking the person assigned what they tested and on which device. show me the issue and the comment here and post only the ones i allow. never mention anyone else, add customer details or limit who can see a comment unless i ask.
routine.needs: jira connected with read and write access for this bot
routine.output:
comment proposal for pay-73
what did you test, and on which device?
no mentions or customer details. no visibility restriction requested.
post this question to pay-73?

steps: connect jira with read and write access so the bot can add comments.
set **sending on your behalf** to **ask every time**. try one comment on an issue you can inspect.
careful with **Full access**: a bot there with no sending rule can send up to 25 a day without asking. give it **Ask every time**.
read the issue, audience and links before **allow**. schedule the weekly review once that looks right.
watch: **group restrictions need setup.** an administrator must enable them. role and group names can differ between projects.
**bare web addresses won't become clickable.** ask for links with descriptive words.
**use ask every time to review each comment.** a daily sending amount lets comments go out within that limit.
**put the update on the right issue.** match the project as well as the title.

faq.q: can the bot make a jira comment internal?
faq.a: **it can request a role or group restriction.** those names must fit your jira setup. ask it to confirm the audience before posting.

faq.q: can it mention a teammate in the comment?
faq.a: **yes, by username or display name.** ask for the mention only when you mean it. review the person alongside the proposed text.

faq.q: does it support a test checklist?
faq.a: **yes, with lists and emphasis.** say what passed, what failed and what nobody tried. give the next tester something they can repeat.

sources.label: Metal docs: sending and approval settings

steps: name one issue and the test result
ask for a comment draft without posting
read who can see the comment and open its evidence links
approve only the comment you read

mistakes.mistake: writing 'tested' with no device or result
mistakes.fix: say what you tried, where you tried it and what happened.
confirm the project role or group. stop if it can't apply the restriction.

tip.text: "tested on my phone" leaves everyone guessing. name the device, steps and result.

items: the issue belongs to the right project
observed and expected results stay separate
links have words people can click
mentions and audience match your intent
